result:
Review complete — **rejected**, tier1.

The diff correctly fixes the three round-3 bugs it claims to fix (spoofable cgroup config file, `+master` force-push, multi-refspec), verified those hold up. But both wrapper scripts detect the guarded operation by checking only `argv[1]`/`argv[2]`, so any git/gh global flag placed before the subcommand walks straight past detection. I live-reproduced three bypasses against the actual shipped snippet:

- `git -C /tmp push origin master` → real git invoked, exit 0, no block
- `git --git-dir=/tmp/.git push origin master` → same
- `gh --repo some/repo pr merge 1 --merge` → same

These are ordinary, everyday command forms (not exotic tricks), none are covered by the test suite, and none are disclosed in the PR's own "known limitations" section. Since this is tier1 (approval means autonomous merge) and the task's whole purpose is closing gate bypasses, I rejected rather than approve a version with a newly-found, easily-triggered bypass class. I also flagged a lower-confidence architectural concern about `systemd --user` cgroup spoofing given the doc's own description of how worker units are launched, though I didn't reproduce that one live.

`review-verdict.json` written to the workspace root with the full findings.
